efficiency_policy.backlog_provenance: Migration-on-touch only: patch backlog/provenance when future dispatch state changes; otherwise record none-with-reason in event/packet.
efficiency_policy.batch_adjacent_increments: One invocation may complete multiple increments when lane/subsystem, source-basis family, verifier surface, and dirty working set stay coherent; stop at gates/failures/subsystem switches/risk/checkpoint/cap boundaries.
efficiency_policy.external_reporting: Report externally only for gates, failures, checkpoint commits/pushes, fidelity promotion/demotion, explicit user request, or periodic batch summaries; routine increments stay local.
efficiency_policy.git_publication: Workers/continuous runners may create local checkpoint commits when needed, but only the integration owner pushes. This preserves batched git savings while avoiding worker credential/auth gate loops.
efficiency_policy.ledger_events: Use compact JSONL events for routine history; rewrite ledger only for changed resumable state, gates, next action, runner policy, or verification summaries.
efficiency_policy.runner_self_inspection: Treat continuous-runner.lock as known wrapper state; do not inspect/wait on the wrapper from inside runner invocations.
efficiency_policy.skill_context: Avoid paying the full skill-token/startup cost every fresh invocation; rely on embedded runner prompt and durable repo artifacts for routine Lane A/source-mining work.
efficiency_policy.verification: Use narrow per-increment verifiers; broad hygiene/full suites/remote checks at checkpoint, handoff, risky-step, or touched-surface boundaries.
efficiency_policy.workers: Avoid workers/subagents for mechanical sequential lanes; use them only for independent parallel lanes where fan-in cost is justified.
